_format: Weekly roundup. Cover still, five video items, closing still. Each item's footage is OF the thing described — that is the format, and an animated version of our own text is not it.
subline: Three of them were robots. One of them was funny.
image_prompts: Cinematic 3D render, a humanoid robot in a sprinter's starting blocks on a stadium track at night, floodlights raking across wet tartan, steam rising, shot from ground level on a 35mm lens, dramatic rim light, near-black background, moody and photographic, no text, no logos

Cinematic 3D render, an empty stadium track at dawn with a single pair of robot running blades left at the finish line, long shadows, volumetric haze, shallow depth of field, near-black background, quiet and cinematic, no text, no logos

items.headline: A robot broke Usain Bolt's 100m record
items.body: X-Humanoid's TienKung Ultra ran it in 9.39 seconds at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing — under the 9.58 Bolt set in 2009. Different rules, same clock.

items.headline: Then four of them ran straight into a barrier
items.body: Same Games, blade-footed sprinters at full speed. The leader flipped through the air in a shower of sparks. Balance is still the hard part.

items.headline: One buried a free kick and hit the SIUUU
items.body: A humanoid scored, then ran the Ronaldo celebration on its own. The Games are really a test of balance, coordination and autonomous movement — the showboating is a side effect.

items.headline: Someone built an India delivery-driver simulator with AI video
items.body: A Chinese creator generated a GTA-style India where you're a delivery rider trying to survive one order. Entirely AI video. Chaotic, and closer to home than most of these demos get.

items.headline: Apple's $899 Mac mini is now an AI machine
items.body: The M6 mini landed this week: 4x the AI performance of the M4, a dual 16-core Neural Engine, 170GB/s bandwidth. Priced at the point where running models locally stops being a flex.

caption:
Five things AI actually did this week.

1. TienKung Ultra ran the 100m in 9.39s at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing — faster than Bolt's 9.58.
2. Four sprinters piled into the barrier at full speed.
3. One scored a free kick and did the SIUUU.
4. A Chinese creator built an India delivery-driver simulator entirely out of AI video.
5. Apple's M6 Mac mini arrived at $899 with 4x the AI performance of the M4.

Which one are you still thinking about?

Footage via @evolving.ai and @askgpts, from the World Humanoid Robot Games broadcast and the original creators.
